title: Symmetry of the same-partition relation
statement: Fix $n \in \bbn$, and regard a union-find state on $n$ nodes as a function $\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbn$ assigning each node a representative. If two such states $\mathit{uf}_1$ and $\mathit{uf}_2$ induce the same partition — that is, for all nodes $i, j$ one has $\mathit{uf}_1(i) = \mathit{uf}_1(j)$ if and only if $\mathit{uf}_2(i) = \mathit{uf}_2(j)$ — then $\mathit{uf}_2$ and $\mathit{uf}_1$ likewise induce the same partition.
hypotheses_covered: uf1 and uf2 induce the same partition on the n nodes
